newsitem.title: USA: Amgen sees '96, '97 net above forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Amgen sees '96, '97 net above forecasts.

text.p: Amgen Inc, which realized a $0.03 per share tax benefit in the third quarter, expects a lower tax rate going forward to push its 1996 and 1997 earnings above forecasts, analysts said.

Analysts, who spoke in a conference call to the comany's chairman Gordon Binder after earnings were released, said Binder forecast 1996 earnings of $2.37 to $2.42 per share. That compares with a First Call estimate of $2.34, and actual 1995 earnings of $1.90 per share.
Binder also forecast 1997 earnings of $2.70 to $2.80 per share, up from prior forecasts of $2.60 to $2.70, analysts said.
They said Amgen cited as the reason for the increased forecast a favorable ruling that lowers the tax rate at its Puerto Rican manufacturing plant.
That adjustment will lower the company's overall tax rate going forward to abut 28 percent from 31 percent, according to Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Robert LeBoyer.
